-- **A routine `brew upgrade` took prod down for ~3 weeks by replacing the
-  daemon's `node` and `op` binaries — three distinct failure modes, one trigger**
-  (2026-08-19 incident, bd `meal-planner-93k`; my *first* diagnosis here blamed
-  an ekreader cert rotation and was wrong — recorded so the mistake isn't
-  repeated). On **Aug 1** `brew` bumped `node` 26.5.0 → 26.5.1 (**deleting** the
-  26.5.0 binary) and `1password-cli`, near the macOS 26.5.2 upgrade. That one
-  event caused, in sequence:
-  1. **Ghost-binary TCC failure.** The daemon had run since Jul 26 on node
-     26.5.0; after Aug 1 that process held a binary no longer on disk. macOS TCC
-     can't validate a deleted binary, so the daemon's calendar (`ekreader`, exit
-     3) and Notes (`osascript -1743`) reads began failing on the next weekly run
-     (Aug 2). **This was the "calendar failing" symptom — not the ekreader
-     grant.** ekreader reads the calendar fine (verified 20 real events); its
-     grant was never broken. A running daemon can silently rot the moment
-     `brew` deletes the binary underneath it, while `git`/`ps` look normal.
-  2. **Gatekeeper block on the fresh binaries.** Restarting to clear the ghost
-     surfaced that the freshly-installed, *quarantined* node 26.5.1 and op were
-     blocked by macOS `AppleSystemPolicy` ("Security policy would not allow
-     process"). `op` hung spawning its `op-daemon` child (all threads parked in
-     `__psynch_cvwait`, zero output), so secrets-load timed out at 15s and the
-     daemon crash-looped. **Fix: approve *both* `op` and `node` in Privacy &
-     Security** — the launchd daemon's own main binary (`node`) needs approval,
-     not just the tool it shells out to. This op breakage was latent since ~Aug
-     1: the daemon would have died on *any* reboot regardless; the restart
-     merely surfaced it.
-  3. **Voided per-binary TCC grants.** TCC keys Automation/Calendar grants to
-     the exact Cellar path/cdhash, so node 26.5.1 inherits none of node
-     26.5.0's grants. node 26.5.1 lacked Full Disk Access until
-     2026-09-27 (`notes-tags: could not open NoteStore … unable to open
-     database file` every run; only the tag refresh was skipped). FDA is now
-     granted (TCC.db `auth_value=2`); the Oct 4 run is the first real proof.
-  **Prevention now in place:** `brew pin node` + `brew pin 1password-cli` so a
-  background `brew upgrade` can't silently replace them again. Diagnostic
-  reflex for "op hangs": `sample <pid>` a stuck process (no sudo needed) and
-  grep the system log for `AppleSystemPolicy` — that's what pinned it to
-  Gatekeeper. And note the failure was *invisible from the outside*: the daemon
-  kept posting a degraded (static all-FULL, no-dedup) plan and only the alert
-  log showed it — read `logs/meal-planner.err.log`, don't trust "it still
-  posted."
+- **A `brew upgrade` replacing the daemon's binaries causes three distinct
+  failures** (Aug 2026, bd `93k`; full detail in bd memory
+  `ops-eventkit-calendar-works-under-launchd`). (1) **Ghost binary:** a running
+  daemon whose node was deleted on disk fails every TCC check (ekreader exit 3,
+  Notes `-1743`) while `ps`/`git` look normal. My first diagnosis blamed an
+  ekreader cert rotation and was wrong. (2) **Gatekeeper:** freshly installed,
+  quarantined `node`/`op` got blocked by `AppleSystemPolicy`; `op` hung (threads
+  in `__psynch_cvwait`) and the daemon crash-looped. Approve *both* binaries in
+  Privacy & Security. Diagnose with `sample <pid>` plus a syslog grep for
+  `AppleSystemPolicy`. (3) **Voided grants:** a new node path inherits no FDA or
+  Automation grants. Throughout, the daemon kept posting degraded plans, so read
+  `logs/meal-planner.err.log`; don't trust "it still posted." The `brew pin`
+  "prevention" chosen then was wrong (next entry).
+
+- **Homebrew node is unsafe for prod both pinned and unpinned (2026-11-18,
+  bd `uzt`, decision `ekd`).** It degraded silently a second time: from Oct 18
+  every weekly run failed recipe sync (Notes `-1743`, then `-1712` timeouts) and
+  the calendar read. Two causes: node was replaced Oct 12 (→26.11.1, despite the
+  pin), and macOS 27.2 dropped ekreader's grant. While we were fixing that, a
+  brew upgrade *that afternoon* replaced `simdjson`/`simdutf`. The pinned node
+  links their old versioned dylibs, so it **could no longer start** (`dyld:
+  Library not loaded`). The running daemon survived only because it still had
+  the deleted dylib mapped; any restart would have crash-looped before our boot
+  guard could run. So the trade is: an unpinned node voids TCC grants on every
+  upgrade (it's ad-hoc signed, so grants key on its cdhash), and a pinned node
+  breaks when its deps move. Also: `1password-cli` is a **cask**, and
+  `brew pin` silently doesn't apply to casks. Fix was unpin + `brew upgrade
+  node` (26.13.1; native-module ABI 147 unchanged, no rebuild) plus re-grants.
+  Diagnostics that found it: run the binary directly; `otool -L <bin>` and
+  test each path exists; `vmmap <pid>` shows the deleted dylib still mapped.

content.text:
There are two separate causes, and neither is stray work.

**1. `.beads/hooks/*`: Entire rewrote the git hooks when you enabled it (16:45).**
- `core.hooksPath` points at `.beads/hooks/`, which is tracked in git. So `entire enable` installed its hooks into that tracked folder.
- It replaced `pre-push` and `prepare-commit-msg` with its own wrappers. It saved the beads originals as `*.pre-entire`, and I checked that those match the committed files exactly. The wrappers run Entire's hook first and then call the beads hook, so beads still runs.
- It also added `commit-msg`, `post-commit` and `post-rewrite`, which only run Entire.
- Your "Enable Entire" commit (`0ccd036`) included `.claude/settings.json` and `.entire/`, but not these hook files. That's why they're still showing as changed.

**2. `.claude/REFLECTIONS.md`: this edit was left out of the last commit.**
- The file was changed at 17:10:07, and `8b4fd1b` ("docs: session-end notes (TCC launchd probe, never brew pin node)") was made 47 seconds later.
- That commit contains only `CLAUDE.md`, but its message describes exactly what's in this diff:
  - a new "Homebrew node is unsafe pinned or unpinned" entry
  - a new "verify TCC in the daemon's context" entry
  - shorter versions of the Aug-incident and beads-state entries
  - a new open question about why silent failures go unnoticed for weeks

**Recommendation:**
- **REFLECTIONS.md:** commit it as the rest of that session-end commit.
- **Hooks:**
  - **Committing them** means every clone gets Entire's hook wrappers. A clone without Entire installed is fine: the wrappers just skip it, and `commit-msg` prints a note saying so.
  - **Leaving them uncommitted** keeps the tree dirty.
  - **Either way:** if `bd hooks install` regenerates the hooks later, it may overwrite Entire's wrappers.

Should I commit both (through a PR, per the repo workflow), or only the reflections?
